en.greeting: Hi! Today you write real messages: your news for a friend, a polite email to your boss, and a short story about your weekend. Let's start with the shape of a message.

steps.title: Four parts of a message
steps.text: A short message to a friend is like a mini conversation. It has four parts.
steps.body:
1. **Greeting**: *Hi Sari!* (Hi + name, then ! or a comma)
2. **News**: something that happened, so the verb is **past**: *Guess what? I passed my driving test!*
3. **A question back**: *How are you?* A message with only your news sounds like you don't care about your friend.
4. **Ending + name**: *See you soon, Rina* (comma before the name).

**Guess what?** (coba tebak!) is a fixed phrase to start news. Capitals and full stops work as in your A1 messages.

steps.title: Budi's message
steps.text: Budi writes to his friend Dimas on WhatsApp. Find the four parts.
steps.body: Greeting → news (*started*: past, + **-ed**) → a question back (*Did you watch…?*: did + base verb) → ending + name. *My boss is really nice* is in the present because it's true now.

examples.en: Hi Dimas!
examples.id: Hai Dimas!

examples.en: Guess what? I started my new job at a bank on Monday!
examples.id: Coba tebak! Aku mulai kerja baru di bank hari Senin!

examples.en: My boss is really nice.
examples.id: Bosku baik banget.

examples.en: How are you? Did you watch the match on Saturday?
examples.id: Apa kabar? Kamu nonton pertandingannya hari Sabtu?

examples.en: Take care, Budi
examples.id: Jaga diri ya, Budi

steps.title: Friend or boss?
steps.text: Now the same kind of message to your boss, a teacher or a client.
steps.body: With friends you can be **informal** (santai): *Hi*, *Thanks!*, *btw*, an emoji or two. With a boss you are **formal** (sopan): **Dear** + Pak/Bu/Mr + name, words in full, no emoji, and **Best wishes,** or **Kind regards,** before your name. Indonesian trap: keep **Pak/Bu** (*Dear Pak Hasan,*), don't write only the first name, and don't end a work email with *Bye bye*. (*Mr Brown* is British; American English writes *Mr.*)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: You start a new job on Monday. You write your first email to your manager.

question.prompt: You're writing an email to your new manager, Bu Ratna. Which opening is best?
question.explanation: To a manager, use **Dear + Bu/Pak + name + comma**: **Dear Bu Ratna,**. 'Hey Ratna! 😊' is for friends (no Bu, an emoji), and 'Bye bye' is an ending, not an opening.

steps.title: News in the past, then ask back
steps.text: Your news already happened, so the verb goes into the past. Then you ask something back.
steps.body:
Indonesian chat only adds a time word (*Kemarin aku lulus ujian*). English changes the verb too: *Yesterday I **passed** my test*, not 'Yesterday I pass'. Irregular verbs have their own past: *got, had, bought, went*. Don't use *was* as a past marker: not 'I was buy'.

Ask back with **How was…?** or **Did you / What did you + base verb**: *What did you buy?*, not 'What did you bought?'. When a friend gives news, react first: *Congratulations!*

pairs.en: Did you have a good time?

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina has big news for her friend.

options: Guess what? I get a new job last week!
Guess what? I got a new job last week!
Guess what? I was get a new job last week!
question.explanation: **last week** is the past, and **get** is irregular: its past is **got**. 'I get' is the present, and 'was get' is wrong because was can't be a past marker for another verb.

steps.title: Build the question
steps.text: Your friend wrote about her weekend. Ask her what she did.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kamu ngapain hari Minggu?
question.solution: What did you do on Sunday?
question.explanation: A past question with a question word: **What + did + you + base verb**: **What did you do on Sunday?** Here *did* is the helper and *do* means 'melakukan'. Not 'What you did…?': English needs *did* before *you*.

steps.title: A 47-word story
steps.text: Now a short story. Sari wrote about her Sunday in 47 words.
steps.body: **Start**: when, where, who. **Middle**: 2–3 things in order, with time words (*in the morning, at one o'clock*). **End**: how it was. **Every verb is past**: *went, took, rented, had, was, came*. Ideas are joined with **and** and **but**. Words like *then* and *so* come in a later lesson. Count everything between spaces: 35–50 words.

examples.en: Last Sunday Budi and I went to Kota Tua in Jakarta.
examples.id: Minggu lalu aku dan Budi pergi ke Kota Tua di Jakarta.

examples.en: We took the KRL train in the morning.
examples.id: Kami naik KRL pagi-pagi.

examples.en: We rented old bikes and took a lot of photos.
examples.id: Kami menyewa sepeda tua dan mengambil banyak foto.

examples.en: At one o'clock we had lunch, but the restaurant was very busy.
examples.id: Jam satu kami makan siang, tapi restorannya ramai sekali.

examples.en: We came home tired but happy.
examples.id: Kami pulang capek tapi senang.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dewi is writing a story about her trip last Saturday. One sentence is wrong.

question.prompt: Which sentence does NOT fit a story about last Saturday?
options: We went to Pangandaran by bus.
We play volleyball on the beach.
We had grilled fish for dinner.
question.explanation: In a story about last Saturday **every verb is past**: *went, had*. 'We play' slips back into the present; it should be **We played volleyball on the beach.**

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for your next message.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · short messages
artifact.intro: The four parts of a message, friend or boss, and how to write a 35–50 word story.
rows: Dear Pak Hasan, / Dear Mr Brown,
Guess what? I passed my test!
How are you? How was your trip?
See you soon, / Love, / Take care,
tips: News and stories: the verb is past, not just the time word: *Yesterday I passed*, not 'Yesterday I pass'.
Questions back: **Did you / What did you + base verb**: *Did you see…?*, not 'Did you saw…?'.
Story: start (when, where, who) → 2–3 things with time words → how it was. 35–50 words; join with and, but, because.

examples.en: Guess what? We moved to Bekasi on Saturday!
examples.id: Coba tebak! Kami pindah ke Bekasi hari Sabtu!

examples.en: Did you see Rina at the wedding?
examples.id: Kamu ketemu Rina di nikahan?

examples.en: Last Friday I went to a concert with Sari.
examples.id: Jumat lalu aku nonton konser bersama Sari.

examples.en: We were tired but happy.
examples.id: Kami capek tapi senang.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu menulis pesan sungguhan: kabarmu untuk teman, email sopan untuk atasan, dan cerita pendek tentang akhir pekanmu. Kita mulai dari bentuk sebuah pesan.

steps.title: Empat bagian pesan
steps.text: Pesan singkat untuk teman itu seperti percakapan mini. Ada empat bagian.
steps.body:
1. **Salam pembuka**: *Hi Sari!* (Hi + nama, lalu ! atau koma)
2. **Kabar**: sesuatu yang sudah terjadi, jadi kata kerjanya **lampau**: *Guess what? I passed my driving test!*
3. **Pertanyaan balik**: *How are you?* Pesan yang isinya hanya kabarmu terdengar seperti kamu tidak peduli pada temanmu.
4. **Penutup + nama**: *See you soon, Rina* (koma sebelum nama).

**Guess what?** (coba tebak!) adalah ungkapan tetap untuk memulai kabar. Huruf kapital dan titik sama seperti pesan A1-mu.

steps.title: Pesan dari Budi
steps.text: Budi menulis ke temannya, Dimas, lewat WhatsApp. Temukan keempat bagiannya.
steps.body: Salam pembuka → kabar (*started*: lampau, + **-ed**) → pertanyaan balik (*Did you watch…?*: did + kata kerja dasar) → penutup + nama. *My boss is really nice* memakai present karena itu benar sekarang.

examples.en: Hi Dimas!
examples.id: Hai Dimas!

examples.en: Guess what? I started my new job at a bank on Monday!
examples.id: Coba tebak! Aku mulai kerja baru di bank hari Senin!

examples.en: My boss is really nice.
examples.id: Bosku baik banget.

examples.en: How are you? Did you watch the match on Saturday?
examples.id: Apa kabar? Kamu nonton pertandingannya hari Sabtu?

examples.en: Take care, Budi
examples.id: Jaga diri ya, Budi

steps.title: Teman atau atasan?
steps.text: Sekarang pesan yang sama untuk atasan, guru atau klien.
steps.body: Dengan teman kamu boleh **informal** (santai): *Hi*, *Thanks!*, *btw*, satu-dua emoji. Dengan atasan kamu **formal** (sopan): **Dear** + Pak/Bu/Mr + nama, kata-kata lengkap, tanpa emoji, dan **Best wishes,** atau **Kind regards,** sebelum namamu. Jebakan: pertahankan **Pak/Bu** (*Dear Pak Hasan,*), jangan tulis nama depannya saja, dan jangan tutup email kerja dengan *Bye bye*. (*Mr Brown* itu British; bahasa Inggris Amerika menulis *Mr.*)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kamu mulai kerja baru hari Senin. Kamu menulis email pertama untuk manajermu.

question.prompt: Kamu menulis email untuk manajer barumu, Bu Ratna. Salam pembuka mana yang paling tepat?
question.explanation: Untuk manajer, pakai **Dear + Bu/Pak + nama + koma**: **Dear Bu Ratna,**. 'Hey Ratna! 😊' untuk teman (tanpa Bu, pakai emoji), dan 'Bye bye' itu penutup, bukan pembuka.

steps.title: Kabar lampau, lalu tanya balik
steps.text: Kabarmu sudah terjadi, jadi kata kerjanya diubah ke bentuk lampau. Lalu kamu bertanya balik.
steps.body:
Chat bahasa Indonesia hanya menambah kata waktu (*Kemarin aku lulus ujian*). Bahasa Inggris juga mengubah kata kerjanya: *Yesterday I **passed** my test*, bukan 'Yesterday I pass'. Kata kerja tidak beraturan punya bentuk lampau sendiri: *got, had, bought, went*. Jangan pakai *was* sebagai penanda lampau: bukan 'I was buy'.

Tanya balik dengan **How was…?** atau **Did you / What did you + kata kerja dasar**: *What did you buy?*, bukan 'What did you bought?'. Saat teman memberi kabar, tanggapi dulu: *Congratulations!*

pairs.en: Did you have a good time?

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina punya kabar besar untuk temannya.

options: Guess what? I get a new job last week!
Guess what? I got a new job last week!
Guess what? I was get a new job last week!
question.explanation: **last week** itu masa lalu, dan **get** tidak beraturan: bentuk lampaunya **got**. 'I get' itu bentuk sekarang, dan 'was get' salah karena was tidak bisa menjadi penanda lampau untuk kata kerja lain.

steps.title: Susun pertanyaannya
steps.text: Temanmu bercerita tentang akhir pekannya. Tanyakan apa yang dia lakukan.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kamu ngapain hari Minggu?
question.solution: What did you do on Sunday?
question.explanation: Pertanyaan lampau dengan kata tanya: **What + did + you + kata kerja dasar**: **What did you do on Sunday?** Di sini *did* adalah kata bantu dan *do* berarti 'melakukan'. Bukan 'What you did…?': bahasa Inggris butuh *did* sebelum *you*.

steps.title: Cerita 47 kata
steps.text: Sekarang cerita pendek. Sari menulis tentang hari Minggunya dalam 47 kata.
steps.body: **Awal**: kapan, di mana, dengan siapa. **Tengah**: 2–3 kejadian berurutan, dengan kata waktu (*in the morning, at one o'clock*). **Akhir**: bagaimana rasanya. **Semua kata kerja lampau**: *went, took, rented, had, was, came*. Ide digabung dengan **and** dan **but**. Kata seperti *then* dan *so* ada di pelajaran berikutnya. Hitung semua yang dipisah spasi: 35–50 kata.

examples.id: Minggu lalu aku dan Budi pergi ke Kota Tua di Jakarta.

examples.en: We rented old bikes and took a lot of photos.

examples.en: At one o'clock we had lunch, but the restaurant was very busy.
examples.id: Jam satu kami makan siang, tapi restorannya ramai sekali.

examples.en: We came home tired but happy.
examples.id: Kami pulang capek tapi senang.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dewi menulis cerita tentang perjalanannya Sabtu lalu. Satu kalimat salah.

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang TIDAK cocok untuk cerita tentang Sabtu lalu?
options: We went to Pangandaran by bus.
We play volleyball on the beach.
We had grilled fish for dinner.
question.explanation: Dalam cerita tentang Sabtu lalu **semua kata kerja lampau**: *went, had*. 'We play' kembali ke bentuk present; seharusnya **We played volleyball on the beach.**

steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk pesanmu berikutnya.
